A molecule (X) with following structure under mild acidic condition is hydrolysed to produce (Y) and (Z).
Identify the correct statements about (Y) and (Z).
(A) Both (Y) and (Z) have same molar mass.
(B) (Y) and (Z) can be distinguished from each other by $NaHCO_{3}.$
(C) (Y) and (Z) react with HCN with same rates.
(D) (Y) and (Z) undergo addition reaction with 2, 4-DNP.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :

image.alt: Figure for this Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids question

questions.solution:
X is $\mathrm{CH_3{-}CH{=}CH{-}O{-}C(CH_3){=}CH_2}$. Both groups on the oxygen are vinyl groups, so X is an enol ether on each side.
In mild acid, the $\mathrm{C{=}C}$ next to the oxygen is protonated, water adds and the C–O bond breaks. Each vinyl group comes off as an enol, which tautomerises to its carbonyl form.
The propenyl side gives $\mathrm{CH_3CH{=}CH{-}OH \rightarrow CH_3CH_2CHO}$, which is propanal (Y).
The isopropenyl side gives $\mathrm{CH_2{=}C(OH)CH_3 \rightarrow CH_3COCH_3}$, which is propanone (Z).
(A) Both products are $\mathrm{C_3H_6O}$ with $M = 58\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$. True.
(B) Neither compound is acidic enough to release $\mathrm{CO_2}$ with $\mathrm{NaHCO_3}$, so this reagent cannot distinguish them. False.
(C) The aldehyde is less hindered and more electrophilic, so it adds HCN faster than the ketone. The rates are not the same. False.
(D) Both undergo addition followed by elimination with 2,4-DNP, each forming an orange 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazone. True.
Answer: (D) A and D only

Molar ratio $\mathrm{C:O:H}=1:1:1$, so the empirical formula is $\mathrm{CHO}$ with empirical formula mass $12+1+16=29\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$.
$n=\dfrac{58}{29}=2$, so the molecular formula is $\mathrm{C_2H_2O_2}$.
$\mathrm{C_2H_2O_2}$ is glyoxal, $\mathrm{OHC{-}CHO}$, which has no α-hydrogen.
Key concept: a dialdehyde with no α-H undergoes an intramolecular Cannizzaro reaction with 50% $\mathrm{KOH}$. One $\mathrm{{-}CHO}$ group is oxidised to $\mathrm{{-}COO^-}$ and the other is reduced to $\mathrm{{-}CH_2OH}$.
$$\mathrm{OHC{-}CHO \xrightarrow{50\%\ KOH} HOCH_2{-}COO^-K^+ \xrightarrow{H_3O^+} HOCH_2{-}COOH}$$
The product is glycolic acid, $\mathrm{HO{-}CH_2{-}COOH}$, which matches option (C).
Answer: (C) $\mathrm{HOCH_2{-}COOH}$ (glycolic acid)

questions.stem:
Match List - I with List - II.
List-I ReagentsList - II
Reaction Name (Involving aldehydes)A. $H _2, Pd - BaSO _4$
B. $SnCl _2, HCl$
C. $CrO _2 Cl _2, CS _2$
D. $CO , HCl$, Anhyd. $AlCl _3$I. Etard Reaction
II. Rosenmund Reduction
III. Gattermann-Koch Reaction
IV. Stephen Reaction Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
A: $\mathrm{H_2,\ Pd{-}BaSO_4}$ partially reduces an acid chloride to an aldehyde: $\mathrm{RCOCl + H_2 \xrightarrow{Pd-BaSO_4} RCHO + HCl}$. This is the Rosenmund reduction, so A → II.
B: $\mathrm{SnCl_2,\ HCl}$ reduces a nitrile to an imine, and hydrolysis of the imine gives an aldehyde: $\mathrm{RCN \to RCH{=}NH \xrightarrow{H_3O^+} RCHO}$. This is the Stephen reaction, so B → IV.
C: Chromyl chloride, $\mathrm{CrO_2Cl_2}$ in $\mathrm{CS_2}$, oxidises toluene to a chromium complex, and hydrolysis of the complex gives benzaldehyde. This is the Etard reaction, so C → I.
D: $\mathrm{CO,\ HCl}$ with anhydrous $\mathrm{AlCl_3}$ (or CuCl) converts benzene into benzaldehyde. This is the Gattermann–Koch reaction, so D → III.
So the matching is A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III.
Answer: (D)

questions.stem:
Match the LIST-I with LIST-II
List-I Reagents List-II Name of Reaction involving carbonyl compounds A. $NH _2- NH _2, KOH$ I. Tollen's Test B. $Ag ( NH _3) _2 OH$ II. Clemmensen Reduction C. Aq. $CuSO _4$, Sodium Potassium tartarate, KOH III. Wolff - Kishner Reduction D. $Zn - Hg , HCl$ IV. Fehling's Test
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
A: $\mathrm{NH_2{-}NH_2}$ first forms a hydrazone with the $\mathrm{C{=}O}$ group. Heating with $\mathrm{KOH}$ then gives $\mathrm{>CH_2}$ and releases $\mathrm{N_2}$. This is the Wolff–Kishner reduction, so A → III.
B: $\mathrm{[Ag(NH_3)_2]OH}$ is Tollens' reagent. It oxidises aldehydes, and a silver mirror forms. This is Tollens' test, so B → I.
C: Aqueous $\mathrm{CuSO_4}$ is Fehling's solution A. Sodium potassium tartrate with $\mathrm{KOH}$ is Fehling's solution B. With aliphatic aldehydes they give a red precipitate of $\mathrm{Cu_2O}$. This is Fehling's test, so C → IV.
D: $\mathrm{Zn{-}Hg}$ with concentrated $\mathrm{HCl}$ reduces $\mathrm{>C{=}O}$ to $\mathrm{>CH_2}$. This is the Clemmensen reduction, so D → II.
So the matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.
Answer: (B)

questions.stem: The compound $A , C _8 H _8 O _2$ reacts with acetophenone to form a single product via cross-Aldol condensation. The compound A on reaction with conc. NaOH forms a substituted benzyl alcohol as one of the two products. The compound $A$ is :
questions.solution:
Key idea: for A to give a single cross-aldol product with acetophenone, A must have no $\alpha$-H, so it cannot enolise and self-condense. Only acetophenone forms the enolate.
For A to undergo the Cannizzaro reaction with conc. NaOH (giving a benzyl alcohol plus a carboxylate), A must be an aromatic aldehyde with no $\alpha$-H.
Check the molecular formula $\mathrm{C_8H_8O_2}$ for each option:
(A) 2-hydroxyacetophenone, $\mathrm{C_8H_8O_2}$: it is a ketone with $\alpha$-H (the $\mathrm{CH_3}$), so it can self-condense and cannot undergo Cannizzaro. Rejected.
(B) 4-hydroxybenzaldehyde, $\mathrm{HO{-}C_6H_4{-}CHO}$, is $\mathrm{C_7H_6O_2}$, so the formula does not match. Rejected.
(C) 4-methylbenzoic acid, $\mathrm{C_8H_8O_2}$: it is an acid, so it gives neither aldol condensation nor Cannizzaro. Rejected.
(D) 4-methoxybenzaldehyde, $\mathrm{CH_3O{-}C_6H_4{-}CHO}$, is $\mathrm{C_8H_8O_2}$ and has no $\alpha$-H. Its cross-aldol with acetophenone gives a single product, the chalcone $\mathrm{CH_3O{-}C_6H_4{-}CH{=}CH{-}CO{-}C_6H_5}$.
Cannizzaro of (D): $2\,\mathrm{CH_3OC_6H_4CHO} + \mathrm{NaOH} \rightarrow \mathrm{CH_3OC_6H_4CH_2OH} + \mathrm{CH_3OC_6H_4COONa}$. One product is 4-methoxybenzyl alcohol, a substituted benzyl alcohol.
Answer: (D) 4-methoxybenzaldehyde

questions.stem: ' $x$ ' is the product which is obtained from propanenitrile and stannous chloride in the presence of hydrochloric acid followed by hydrolysis. ' $y$ ' is the product which is obtained from the but-2-ene by the ozonolysis followed by hydrolysis. From the following, which product is not obtained when one mole of ' $x$ ' and one mole of ' $y$ ' react with each other in the presence of alkali followed by heating?
questions.solution:
Key concepts: the Stephen reduction turns a nitrile into an aldehyde. Ozonolysis splits a C=C bond into two carbonyl compounds. Two different aldehydes that both have α‑H give a crossed aldol condensation, which forms four products.
Step 1 – Find $x$ (Stephen reduction): $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2C{\equiv}N \xrightarrow{SnCl_2/HCl} CH_3CH_2CH{=}NH\cdot HCl \xrightarrow{H_2O} CH_3CH_2CHO}$. So $x$ = propanal.
Step 2 – Find $y$ (ozonolysis): $\mathrm{CH_3CH{=}CHCH_3 \xrightarrow{O_3,\ Zn/H_2O} 2\,CH_3CHO}$. So $y$ = ethanal.
Step 3 – Both aldehydes have α‑H. With dilute alkali and heat they give a crossed aldol condensation, which produces four α,β‑unsaturated aldehydes.
Step 4 – Propanal + propanal (self condensation): $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH{=}C(CH_3)CHO}$ = 2‑methylpent‑2‑enal (A).
Step 5 – Ethanal + ethanal (self condensation): $\mathrm{CH_3CH{=}CHCHO}$ = but‑2‑enal.
Step 6 – The carbanion from ethanal attacks the C=O of propanal: $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH{=}CHCHO}$ = pent‑2‑enal (D).
Step 7 – The carbanion from propanal attacks the C=O of ethanal: $\mathrm{CH_3CH{=}C(CH_3)CHO}$ = 2‑methylbut‑2‑enal (B).
Step 8 – 3‑Methylbut‑2‑enal is $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2C{=}CHCHO}$. Making it would need acetone as the carbonyl partner, and acetone is not present. So this product cannot form.
Answer: (C) 3‑Methylbut‑2‑enal

questions.stem: From the given following (A to D) cyclic structures, those which will not react with Tollen's reagent are:

image.alt: Figure for this Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids question

questions.solution:
Key idea: Tollens' reagent oxidises only a free –CHO group. A cyclic sugar can give –CHO only if its anomeric carbon is a hemiacetal (free $\mathrm{-OH}$ and ring $\mathrm{O}$ on the same carbon), because the ring then opens to the aldehyde in base.
If the anomeric $\mathrm{-OH}$ is replaced by $\mathrm{-OCH_3}$, the carbon is an acetal (a glycoside). It is stable in base, cannot open, and does not reduce Tollens' reagent.
Structure A: the anomeric carbon has a free $\mathrm{-OH}$. It is a hemiacetal, so it reacts and gives a silver mirror.
Structure D: the anomeric carbon has a free $\mathrm{-OH}$. It is a hemiacetal, so it reacts.
Structure B: the anomeric carbon has $\mathrm{-OCH_3}$ (a methyl glucoside). It is an acetal and does not react.
Structure C: the anomeric carbon of the furanose ring has $\mathrm{-OCH_3}$. It is an acetal and does not react.
Answer: (D) B and C

questions.stem: The correct sequence of reagents for the above conversion of $X$ to $Y$ is :

image.alt: Figure for this Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids question

questions.solution:
The $-\mathrm{COOH}$ in $Y$ is on the former terminal $\mathrm{CH_3}$ carbon, so the functional group must move from the benzylic carbon to the terminal carbon.
(i) NaOEt (strong base) causes E2 elimination: $\mathrm{C_6H_5CH(Br)CH_3 \rightarrow C_6H_5CH{=}CH_2}$ (styrene).
(ii) $\mathrm{B_2H_6}$ then $\mathrm{H_2O_2/OH^-}$ gives anti-Markovnikov hydration: $\mathrm{C_6H_5CH{=}CH_2 \rightarrow C_6H_5CH_2CH_2OH}$.
(iii) Jones reagent oxidises the primary alcohol to the acid: $\mathrm{C_6H_5CH_2CH_2OH \rightarrow C_6H_5CH_2COOH}$ ($Y$).
(A) fails: aqueous NaOH gives a secondary alcohol, which Jones oxidises to acetophenone.
(C) fails: Jones reagent does not act on $X$, and hot $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$ gives benzoic acid.
(D) fails: $\mathrm{B_2H_6}$ cannot act on $X$ because it has no C=C bond.
Answer: B

questions.stem:
Which of the following statements are TRUE about Haloform reaction?
A. Sodium hypochlorite reacts with KI to give KOI .
B. KOI is a reducing agent.
C. $\alpha, \beta$-unsaturated methylketone will give iodoform reaction.
D. Isopropyl alcohol will not give iodoform test.
E. Methanoic acid will give positive iodoform test.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :

image.alt: Figure for this Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids question

questions.solution:
Concept: In the iodoform test, $\mathrm{I_2}$ or hypoiodite ($\mathrm{OI^-}$) is formed in the presence of base. It oxidises and iodinates a $\mathrm{CH_3CO{-}}$ group, or a $\mathrm{CH_3CH(OH){-}}$ group that can be oxidised to $\mathrm{CH_3CO{-}}$, giving yellow $\mathrm{CHI_3}$.
Statement A: $\mathrm{NaOCl + KI \rightarrow KOI + NaCl}$. Hypochlorite oxidises iodide to hypoiodite, so A is true.
Statement B: In $\mathrm{KOI}$, iodine is in the $+1$ state. It oxidises the substrate and is reduced to $\mathrm{I^-}$, so it is an oxidising agent, not a reducing agent. B is false.
Statement C: The figure shows $\mathrm{CH_3{-}CH{=}CH{-}CO{-}CH_3}$. It contains a $\mathrm{CH_3CO{-}}$ group, so it forms $\mathrm{CHI_3}$ and $\mathrm{CH_3CH{=}CHCOO^-}$. C is true.
Statement D: Isopropyl alcohol, $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2CHOH}$, is oxidised to acetone, $\mathrm{CH_3COCH_3}$, which gives iodoform. So it gives a positive test, and D is false.
Statement E: Methanoic acid, $\mathrm{HCOOH}$, has neither a $\mathrm{CH_3CO{-}}$ group nor a $\mathrm{CH_3CH(OH){-}}$ group, so it gives a negative test. E is false.
The true statements are A and C.
Answer: (D) A & C Only

questions.stem: lodoform test can differentiate between A. Methanol and Ethanol B. $CH _3 COOH$ and $CH _3 CH _2 COOH$ C. Cyclohexene and cyclohexanone D. Diethyl ether and Pentan-3-one E. Anisole and acetone Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Key idea: A compound gives a positive iodoform test ($\mathrm{I_2/NaOH}$, yellow $\mathrm{CHI_3}$) if it contains $\mathrm{CH_3CO{-}}$ (a methyl ketone or acetaldehyde), or $\mathrm{CH_3CH(OH){-}}$ (which is oxidised to $\mathrm{CH_3CO{-}}$). Carboxylic acids do not give the test. The test can tell two compounds apart only if exactly one of them gives it.
A. Ethanol, $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2OH}$, has a $\mathrm{CH_3CH(OH){-}}$ unit, so it gives the test. Methanol, $\mathrm{CH_3OH}$, does not. The test can differentiate this pair.
B. Neither $\mathrm{CH_3COOH}$ nor $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2COOH}$ gives the test, because acids are negative. The test cannot differentiate this pair.
C. Cyclohexene has no carbonyl group. Cyclohexanone is not a methyl ketone. Both are negative, so the test cannot differentiate this pair.
D. Diethyl ether, $\mathrm{C_2H_5OC_2H_5}$, is negative. Pentan-3-one, $\mathrm{C_2H_5COC_2H_5}$, is also negative because it has no $\mathrm{CH_3CO{-}}$ group. The test cannot differentiate this pair.
E. Anisole, $\mathrm{C_6H_5OCH_3}$, is negative. Acetone, $\mathrm{CH_3COCH_3}$, is a methyl ketone and is positive. The test can differentiate this pair.
So only pairs A and E can be told apart by the iodoform test.
Answer: (C) A & E Only

questions.stem: Consider the following two reactions A and B . Numerical value of [molar mass of $x+$ molar mass of $y$ ] is $\text{\_\_\_\_}$

image.alt: Figure for this Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids question

questions.solution:
**Reaction A:** phenol is acidic, so it reacts with the active metal sodium and releases hydrogen gas.
$$2\,\mathrm{C_6H_5OH} + 2\,\mathrm{Na} \rightarrow 2\,\mathrm{C_6H_5ONa} + \mathrm{H_2}\uparrow$$
So gas $x = \mathrm{H_2}$, with molar mass $2\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$.

**Reaction B:** benzoic acid is a stronger acid than carbonic acid, so it reacts with $\mathrm{NaHCO_3}$ and releases carbon dioxide (effervescence).
$$\mathrm{C_6H_5COOH} + \mathrm{NaHCO_3} \rightarrow \mathrm{C_6H_5COONa} + \mathrm{H_2O} + \mathrm{CO_2}\uparrow$$
So gas $y = \mathrm{CO_2}$, with molar mass $12 + 2(16) = 44\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$.

**Sum of molar masses:**
$2 + 44 = 46\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$

Answer: (A) 46

questions.stem:
A student is given one compound among the following compounds that gives positive test with Tollen's reagent.
The compound is :

image.alt: Figure for this Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids question

questions.solution:
Tollens' reagent $\mathrm{[Ag(NH_3)_2]^+}$ oxidises aldehydes. So the compound must have a free $\mathrm{-CHO}$ group, or be able to form one in solution.
Compound A (2-methoxytetrahydrofuran) is a cyclic acetal. Acetals do not open in the basic Tollens' medium, so A gives no free aldehyde and the test is negative.
Compounds B and D are an ordinary cyclic ether and a secondary alcohol. Neither has an aldehyde group, so both give a negative test.
Compound C (2-hydroxytetrahydrofuran) has $\mathrm{-OH}$ and ring $\mathrm{-O-}$ on the same carbon, so it is a cyclic hemiacetal.
In solution, a hemiacetal is in equilibrium with its open-chain form:
$$\text{2-hydroxytetrahydrofuran} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{HO{-}CH_2CH_2CH_2{-}CHO}\ (\text{4-hydroxybutanal})$$
The free $\mathrm{-CHO}$ is oxidised to $\mathrm{-COO^-}$, and $\mathrm{Ag^+}$ is reduced to $\mathrm{Ag}$, which forms a silver mirror. So C gives a positive Tollens' test.
Compound C is option (D).
Answer: D

questions.stem: Grignard reagent $\mathrm{RMgBr} ( P )$ reacts with water and forms a gas $( Q )$. One gram of Q occupies $1.4\ \mathrm{dm}^3$ at STP. (P) on reaction with dry ice in dry ether followed by $\mathrm{H}_3\mathrm{O}^{+}$forms a compound (Z). 0.1 mole of (Z) will weigh $\_\_\_\_$ g. (Nearest integer)
questions.solution:
Key idea: A Grignard reagent gives the alkane $\mathrm{RH}$ with water. It gives the carboxylic acid $\mathrm{RCOOH}$ with $\mathrm{CO_2}$ (dry ice) followed by $\mathrm{H_3O^+}$.
At STP, 1 mol of a gas occupies $22.4\ \mathrm{dm^3}$.
$1\ \mathrm{g}$ of Q occupies $1.4\ \mathrm{dm^3}$, so the molar mass of Q is $M = \dfrac{22.4}{1.4} = 16\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$.
A gas with $M = 16\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$ is methane, so Q is $\mathrm{CH_4}$. Hence $\mathrm{R = CH_3}$ and P is $\mathrm{CH_3MgBr}$.
With water: $\mathrm{CH_3MgBr + H_2O \rightarrow CH_4 + Mg(OH)Br}$.
With dry ice: $\mathrm{CH_3MgBr + CO_2 \xrightarrow{dry\ ether} CH_3COOMgBr \xrightarrow{H_3O^+} CH_3COOH}$.
So Z is acetic acid, $\mathrm{CH_3COOH}$, with $M = 60\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$.
Mass of 0.1 mol of Z $= 0.1 \times 60 = 6\ \mathrm{g}$.
Answer: 6

questions.stem: 'x' is the product which is obtained by the hydrolysis of prop-1-yne in the presence of mercuric sulphate under dilute acidic medium at 333 K. 'y' is the product which is obtained by the reaction of ethane nitrile with methyl magnesium bromide in dry ether followed by hydrolysis. IUPAC name of product obtained from 'x' and 'y' in the presence of barium hydroxide followed by heating is:

An optically active alkyl bromide $C_4H_9Br$, reacts with ethanolic KOH to form major compound [A] which reacts with bromine to give compound [B]. Compound [B] reacts with ethanolic KOH and sodamide to give compound [C]. One molecule of water adds to compound [C] on warming with mercuric sulphate and dilute sulphuric acid at 333 K to form compound [D]. The functional group in compound D will be confirmed by:

'x' is the product which is obtained from benzene by reacting it with carbon monoxide and hydrogen chloride in the presence of cuprous chloride. 'y' is the major product obtained from the benzene by reacting it with ethanoyl chloride in the presence of anhydrous $\mathrm{AlCl}_{3}$. Product (major) obtained by heating x and y in the presence of alkali is z. Total number of π (pi) electrons in z is ______.
questions.solution:
Concepts: Gattermann–Koch reaction, Friedel–Crafts acylation, Claisen–Schmidt (crossed aldol) condensation.
Step 1 (x, Gattermann–Koch): $\mathrm{C_6H_6 + CO + HCl \xrightarrow{AlCl_3/CuCl} C_6H_5CHO}$, so x = benzaldehyde.
Step 2 (y, Friedel–Crafts acylation): $\mathrm{C_6H_6 + CH_3COCl \xrightarrow{AlCl_3} C_6H_5COCH_3}$, so y = acetophenone.
Step 3 (z, Claisen–Schmidt): benzaldehyde has no α‑H. The acetophenone enolate attacks the C=O of benzaldehyde, and heating removes water.
$$\mathrm{C_6H_5CHO + CH_3COC_6H_5 \xrightarrow{OH^-,\ \Delta} C_6H_5CH{=}CH{-}CO{-}C_6H_5 + H_2O}$$
z = benzylideneacetophenone (chalcone).
Step 4 (π bonds in z): two benzene rings give $2\times3 = 6$, C=C gives 1 and C=O gives 1, for a total of 8 π bonds.
Step 5 (π electrons): $8 \times 2 = 16$.
Answer: 16
